newsitem.title: SYRIA: Japan in talks with Syrians over Golan peace force.
newsitem.headline: Japan in talks with Syrians over Golan peace force.

text.p: Syrian President Hafez al-Assad had talks with Japanese Defence Minister Fumio Kyuma on Saturday about extending for two more years the term of Japanese troops in a U.N. peacekeeping force on the Golan Heights.
Spokesman Joubran Kourieh told Reuters that Defence Minister Lieutenant-General Mustafa Tlas was at the meeting at the presidential palace in the Syrian capital.

Japanese Defence Ministry officials told Reuters the Japanese government was expected to extend the term of the 45-member Japanese force, which ends in February, at a cabinet session later this month.

Major-General David Stapleton, commander of the U.N. Disengagement Observer Force (UNDOF) separating Syrian and Israeli troops in the Golan, said he had talks in Damascus with the Japanese defence minister over the Japanese mission.
"I told him that the Japanese unit was doing its job in an excellent way and that we would be pleased to have them for a longer term," he told Reuters.
Stapleton said the Japanese minister inspected the Japanese troops on the Syrian side of the Golan.
He said Kyuma was expected to fly to Cairo later on Saturday and then go to Israel to inspect members of the Japanese unit doing logistics work on the Israeli side of the Golan.
The U.N. commander said the Golan was quiet and Syria and Israel were sticking to terms of a disengagement agreement reached in 1974 after the 1973 Middle East war.
The Japanese unit was sent in February 1996 for a two-year term, the first contribution by Japan to a peacekeeping force in the Middle East.
